title: Power Toys Run: Calculator doesn't handle scientific notation properly
author: lukas-lang

judgment.rationale: The exact expression =0-1e0 and expected -1 make this a controlled calculator regression. Current Command Palette calculator code explicitly rewrites scientific notation and contains scientific-notation tests, but the report specifically targets the legacy PowerToys Run plugin.
evidence: The reporter says =0-1e0 produces 0 rather than -1.
The issue links #39659 and says its prior fix did not cover PowerToys Run.
Current Command Palette CalculateHelper recognizes scientific notation and rewrites it before evaluation.
Current Command Palette unit tests include scientific-notation cases; this does not prove legacy PowerToys Run behavior.
judgment.recommended_action: Reproduce in both the legacy PowerToys Run calculator and Command Palette calculator, then port only the missing parser/evaluator behavior if the legacy path remains wrong.

fix_assessment.rationale: A design should not assume shared calculator code because the current scientific-notation implementation resides in Command Palette while the issue names PowerToys Run.

issue_context.summary: The legacy PowerToys Run calculator may parse a negative scientific-notation term incorrectly, unlike the newer Command Palette calculator path.
known_information: The report supplies the exact expression and expected result.
It points to an earlier related issue.
The current Command Palette calculator has explicit scientific-notation normalization and test coverage.
inferences: The older plugin may lack the newer normalization or bind unary subtraction differently around e notation.
issue_context.analysis: The report is reproducible without reporter follow-up. Comparing the two calculators prevents copying a modern fix into an unrelated engine without confirming the affected boundary.
initial_investigation: Read the complete issue and empty discussion.
Searched live issues for directly matching scientific-notation reports.

reproduce.module: PowerToys Run and Command Palette Calculator
steps: In PowerToys Run, enter =0-1e0 and record the result.
Run the same inputs in Command Palette Calculator.
If only PowerToys Run fails, trace its input normalization before the expression engine.
reproduce.expected_result: Every expression evaluates with 1e0 equal to 1, so =0-1e0 returns -1.
setup_requirements: Use a culture where decimal separator does not alter these integer inputs.
